request: Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.
summary:
I've built your lost-and-found board in `app.py`, and all 14 of my automated tests pass. The tests covered every endpoint and rule in the plan. Items are saved in a file called `lost_and_found.db` in the project folder.

**Endpoints**
- **`POST /items`** adds a found item. You send `description` (what it is), `where_found` and `date_found` (as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. `2024-05-01`). The board gives the item a number and sets its status to "waiting for owner".
- **`GET /items`** lists every item, claimed or not.
- **`GET /items/waiting`** lists only the items still waiting for their owners.
- **`GET /items/{item number}`** shows one item.
- **`POST /items/{item number}/claim`** takes `owner_name`, marks the item as "claimed" and records the owner's name.

**Rules**
- An item can't be added if the description, location or date is missing or blank, or if the date isn't valid.
- An item can't be claimed if the owner's name is missing or blank.
- If someone tries to claim an item that's already claimed, the board refuses and keeps the original owner's name.
- Asking for or claiming an item number that doesn't exist gets an "Item not found" message.

**Two things to know**
- Your two open questions are still unchanged, because the plan left them out. Right now anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed, not just the desk. And anyone who looks at a claimed item can see the owner's name. Let me know if you'd like either one changed.
- The tests save their sample items in the same file as real items, so delete `lost_and_found.db` before you start using the board. The board will create a fresh, empty file the next time it starts.

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple online board for your campus lost-and-found desk. Anyone who finds something can add it to the board with a short description, where it was found and the date it was found. Everyone can see the full list of items, look at a single item, or see only the items still waiting for their owners. When an owner collects an item, the desk marks it as claimed and records the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed a second time. Everything you asked for is included, and nothing in your request was unsafe or outside the backend. Two questions for you to consider (not included in this plan unless you ask): 1) As planned, anyone using the board could mark an item as claimed, not just the desk staff. Would you like only the desk to be able to do this? 2) Owners' names will be visible to anyone who looks at a claimed item. Would you prefer to keep owners' names hidden from the public for privacy?

data.name: Item
fields: Item number (given automatically so each item can be found on its own)
Description (a short description of the item)
Status (either 'waiting for owner' or 'claimed'; starts as 'waiting for owner')
Owner's name (empty until the item is claimed)

endpoints.does: Adds a found item to the board, using its description, where it was found and the date it was found. The item starts as waiting for its owner.
Shows every item on the board, both claimed and still waiting.
Shows only the items that are still waiting for their owners.
Shows one item, chosen by its item number.
Marks one item as claimed when the owner collects it and writes down the owner's name.

rules: A found item cannot be added unless it has a description, where it was found and the date it was found.
An item cannot be marked as claimed unless the owner's name is given.
An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again; the attempt is refused and the original owner's name is kept.
Asking for or claiming an item number that does not exist is refused with a message saying the item was not found.
